title: Structural basis of phospholipid sensing nuclear receptor LRH-1 recognition by carboxylic acid bioisosteres reveals an alternative ligand interaction site.
authors: Bhowmik, Debipreeta; Cato, Michael L; Abraham, Sarah M; Spurlin, Racheal M; Flynn, Autumn R; Colucci, Jennifer K; Mays, Suzanne; D'Agostino, Emma H; Johnson, Alyssa M; Jui, Nathan T; Calvert, John; Ortlund, Eric A
one_liner_zh: 该研究结合晶体结构、分子动力学模拟和突变分析，揭示羧酸生物电子等排体修饰的LRH-1激动剂在配体结合口袋中的动态采样和新型相互作用位点，属于蛋白质-配体结构计算与实验结合研究，但核心对象为核受体配体识别而非通用蛋白结构计算方法创新。
abstract: Liver receptor homolog-1 (LRH-1; NR5A2) is a phospholipid-sensing nuclear receptor that regulates metabolic and steroidogenic pathways in the liver, intestine, and pancreas. Previously, we showed that small-molecule LRH-1 agonists with carboxylic acid "tails" mimic endogenous phospholipid contacts at the mouth of the ligand-binding pocket, enhancing receptor activation. To improve metabolic stability while preserving these key interactions, we designed a series of agonists in which the carboxylate was replaced with bioisosteric polar groups. Substituting a tetrazole for the carboxylate in a lead agonist preserved high affinity LRH-1 binding, improved potency in cellular reporter assays, and promoted stronger target gene induction. Incorporation of a sulfamide moiety to promote interactions in the deep part of the LRH-1 binding pocket yielded a dual-modified agonist (6NTet) with further gains in affinity and activity. Crystal structures, molecular dynamics simulations, and mutational analyses revealed that the 6NTet tetrazole tail dynamically samples two distinct interaction sites within the LRH-1 ligand-binding pocket. One site corresponds to a previously characterized region engaged by phospholipid ligands and synthetic carboxylate-containing agonists (site 1), whereas the second represents a previously unrecognized interaction site (site 2). Mutational analyses demonstrated that both sites contribute to agonist-induced receptor activation, while site 2 additionally influences basal LRH-1 activity. Together, these findings establish tetrazole substitution as an effective strategy for improving phospholipid-mimetic LRH-1 agonists and identify 6NTet as a promising lead compound. The discovery of a novel ligand interaction site further expands our understanding of LRH-1 activation and provides a framework for next-generation agonist design.
abstract_zh: 肝受体同源物-1（LRH-1；NR5A2）是一种磷脂感应核受体，调控肝脏、肠道和胰腺中的代谢及类固醇生成通路。此前，我们展示了带有羧酸“尾部”的小分子LRH-1激动剂模拟内源性磷脂在配体结合口袋口部的接触，增强受体激活。为在保持这些关键相互作用的同时提高代谢稳定性，我们设计了一系列激动剂，其中羧酸被生物电子等排极性基团取代。在一种先导激动剂中，将羧酸替换为四氮唑，保持了高亲和力的LRH-1结合，提高了细胞报告基因实验中的效力，并促进了更强的靶基因诱导。引入磺酰胺部分以促进LRH-1结合口袋深部的相互作用，产生了一种双重修饰的激动剂（6NTet），其亲和力和活性进一步提升。晶体结构、分子动力学 (molecular dynamics) 模拟和突变分析揭示，6NTet的四氮唑尾部在LRH-1配体结合口袋内动态采样两个不同的相互作用位点。一个位点对应于先前表征的、由磷脂配体和含羧酸合成激动剂占据的区域（位点1），而第二个位点代表一个先前未识别的相互作用位点（位点2）。突变分析表明，两个位点均有助于激动剂诱导的受体激活，而位点2还额外影响LRH-1的基础活性。综合这些发现，确立了四氮唑取代作为改善磷脂模拟LRH-1激动剂的有效策略，并将6NTet鉴定为有前景的先导化合物。新配体相互作用位点的发现进一步扩展了我们对LRH-1激活的理解，并为下一代激动剂设计提供了框架。
